prompt: An antiproton is the anti-particle of the proton. It has the same mass as a proton, but has a charge of -1.60 x 10-19 C and is made of antimatter. Whenever matter and antimatter come into contact they will annihilate and convert 100% of their mass into energy. If 120 protons collided with an equal number of antiprotons, the total energy released would be _____ x10-7 J.
judge_reasoning: CONSTRAINT CHECKLIST: (1) compute total energy from 120 protons + 120 antiprotons annihilating with 100% mass-energy; (2) output as coefficient times 10^-7 J. Candidate [1] Pass; [2] Fail; [3] Partial (correct energy magnitude but not the requested coefficient format); [4] Fail. Candidate [1] correctly computes the total converted mass and reports 3.6072e-8 J as 0.361 x10^-7 J. Candidate [2] gives 3.6 x10^-7 J (exponent/format mismatch, wrong by about a factor of 10), candidate [4] overcounts annihilations (14400), producing a vastly too-large energy, and candidate [3] stops at 3.6 x10^-8 J instead of converting to the requested coefficient.
